expectations.text: Identifies SQL injection in GET /orders where req.query.userId is concatenated into the query string (CWE-89)
expectations.evidence: Finding 1 'SQL injection via string interpolation', location GET /orders line 12: 'req.query.userId is concatenated directly into raw SQL via a template literal instead of being passed as a bound parameter.' Cites CWE-89.

expectations.text: Identifies broken access control / IDOR in GET /orders/:id — the order is fetched by id with no check that it belongs to req.user (CWE-639)
expectations.evidence: Finding 6 'Broken access control — any order readable by any authenticated user', GET /orders/:id (lines 18-22): 'there is no ownership/role check — any valid order ID returns the full row to any authenticated caller.' Cites CWE-639.

expectations.text: Identifies mass assignment in PATCH /orders/:id — req.body is passed straight into Order.update, letting the client set fields like status/total/user_id (CWE-915)
expectations.evidence: Finding 7 'Mass assignment — unfiltered request body forwarded to update': 'The entire client-supplied req.body is forwarded to the model update with no allowlist of permitted fields... e.g. total, user_id, paid, or an internal flag.' Cites CWE-915. (Companion Finding 8 separately covers the status field.)

expectations.text: Identifies the unvalidated refund amount in POST /orders/:id/refund — no sign/upper-bound check allows negative or over-refund (business-logic / CWE-839)
expectations.evidence: Finding 3 'Refund amount accepted with no validation': 'no check that it is a positive number, no upper bound... amount: -500 ... amount: 999999 (over-refund beyond the order total).' Cites CWE-839/840.

expectations.text: [PRECISION] Does NOT report the parameterized queries using `$1` placeholders (in GET/PATCH /orders/:id) as SQL injection
expectations.evidence: 'Considered and cleared' section explicitly clears both: 'GET /orders/:id (line 19) and PATCH /orders/:id (line 26) SQL queries — both use $1 bound parameters correctly; no injection here (in contrast to finding 1).'

expectations.text: Flags SHA-256 used for password storage in hash_password — no key stretching, needs bcrypt/argon2id (CWE-916)
expectations.evidence: Finding 3, 'Passwords hashed with unsalted, unstretched SHA-256', hash_password() lines 18-19, explicitly cites CWE-916 (Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort) and recommends Argon2id/bcrypt.

expectations.text: Flags jwt.decode called without an algorithms allowlist in current_user — enables algorithm-confusion / 'none' acceptance (CWE-327/CWE-347)
expectations.evidence: Finding 2, 'JWT decoded without an algorithm allowlist', current_user() line 32, explicitly describes alg:none/HS-RS confusion and cites CWE-347/CWE-327.

expectations.text: Flags the password-reset token generated with uuid.uuid1() as predictable (time/MAC-based, not cryptographically random) (CWE-330)
expectations.evidence: Finding 1, 'Predictable password-reset token (uuid1, not a CSPRNG)', line 41, describes the timestamp/node/clock-sequence structure and cites CWE-640/CWE-330.

expectations.text: Flags verify=False disabling TLS certificate verification on the requests.post billing call (CWE-295)
expectations.evidence: Finding 9, 'TLS certificate verification disabled on outbound billing call', call_billing() line 48, cites CWE-295.

expectations.text: [PRECISION] Does NOT flag hmac.compare_digest in verify_webhook as a timing-unsafe comparison (it is the correct constant-time function)
expectations.evidence: 'Considered and Cleared': 'verify_webhook()... Correct pattern — HMAC-SHA256 with hmac.compare_digest for constant-time comparison. No finding.' The review instead flags login()'s plain `!=` comparison (Finding 8) as the actual non-constant-time issue, explicitly contrasting it with verify_webhook's correct usage — the allowed different/legitimate issue.

expectations.text: [PRECISION] Does NOT flag secrets.token_urlsafe in new_api_key as weak/predictable randomness (it is a correct CSPRNG)
expectations.evidence: 'Considered and Cleared': 'new_api_key()... Correct use of secrets.token_urlsafe(32) — 256 bits of CSPRNG entropy. No finding.'

expectations.text: Flags SSRF in GET /proxy/image — req.query.url is fetched server-side with no scheme/host allowlist or internal-range blocking (CWE-918)
expectations.evidence: Finding 1: 'the url query parameter goes straight into a server-side fetch() with no scheme check, no allowlist, and no private-IP/metadata-IP block' ... 'CWE-918, OWASP A01'.

expectations.text: Flags the user-configurable webhook targetUrl in POST /webhooks stored with no allowlist / SSRF validation (CWE-918)
expectations.evidence: Finding 2: 'targetUrl is stored with zero validation — no scheme check, no allowlist, no private-IP/metadata block ... (CWE-918, OWASP A01)'.

expectations.text: Notes that /proxy/image pipes the upstream response body back to the caller, turning the SSRF into a data-exfiltration / internal-response-disclosure channel
expectations.evidence: Finding 1: 'the raw upstream response (body + content-type) is piped directly back to the caller' and 'streams the response straight back, so the endpoint acts as an anonymous internal-network read oracle / port scanner, with a direct path to cloud-credential theft'.

expectations.text: [PRECISION] Does NOT report GET /assets/:id as SSRF — the host is a fixed internal CDN_BASE and only a validated positive integer id is user-controlled

expectations.text: Flags the hardcoded OpenAI API key passed to OpenAI(api_key=...) (CWE-798)

expectations.evidence: Finding 4 'Indirect Prompt Injection via Unsanitized RAG Context in the Trusted System Message' (lines 33-38, 41): 'Retrieved KB text (docs) and the raw end-user message are concatenated with no delimiter or trust marking into a single blob sent under the system role.' Finding 1's exploit path also demonstrates the direct mechanism: 'message ... is interpolated straight into the prompt ... expectations.text: Flags the hardcoded OpenAI API key passed to OpenAI(api_key=...) (CWE-798)

expectations.evidence: "Considered and cleared": "findUser's knex(...).where({ id: userId }) is parameterized by knex — no SQL injection." (Finding #7 separately flags the row returning unprojected columns — a distinct data-exposure concern, not SQLi.)

expectations.evidence: "Considered and cleared": "tipOfTheDay's Math.random() is used only for cosmetic tip selection, not a security-sensitive value, so non-CSPRNG randomness is fine here."

notes: RECALL TIE (4th consecutive iteration): 26/26 assertions both arms. Standard/easy set, now run on Sonnet 5 instead of the frontier default used in iteration-1 — same tie pattern holds, so the model-tier switch to Sonnet does not by itself surface a skill advantage on textbook vulns.

THOROUGHNESS ~EVEN ON EASY SET: with_skill 40 TP vs without_skill 39 TP (both 0 FP) — a 1-finding edge to the skill, materially a wash. This matches iteration-1's qualitative finding (graders noted the skill arm's extra unrewarded catches on this same easy set).
PRECISION: perfect on both arms (1.00/1.00, 0 FP each) — the easy set doesn't stress precision enough to separate them; see iteration-4 for where a gap appears.

COST: with_skill 1.56x tokens (122.3k vs 78.4k), 1.13x wall-clock. Notably lower time-premium than iteration-1's 1.78x on the same files — Sonnet's baseline reviews took relatively longer on their own, narrowing the skill's relative overhead.
